item.title: Where Are We in the U.S. Economic Cycle? A Spectral Decomposition
item.description: Economic cycles are not one wave but several, superimposed. In Schumpeter’s nesting, one long Kondratieff wave contains roughly six Juglar cycles and eighteen Kitchin cycles; when the components peak together they amplify, and when they offset, they cancel. This note applies that framework to the longest U.S. samples available — industrial production (1919–2026) and real GDP (to 2026 Q3) — using Fourier decomposition with harmonic regression on trailing windows as the primary phase estimator, cross-checked with wavelet analysis.
